candidates.title: Break and recover M2.5 HELICOIL tangs from an ODRI actuator shell
candidates.objective: Use the specified straight tang-break-off mandrel to fracture the tangs of four already-installed M2.5 × 3.75 mm HELICOIL inserts in an actual robot actuator shell, then recover every free tang without damaging the inserts or printed shell.
candidates.success_conditions: Full success requires four contact-driven notch fractures, four independently simulated tang fragments recovered into a tray, no fragment remaining in the shell, no insert displacement, no shell damage, and a stable two-second final inspection. Off-axis loading, insufficient impulse, excessive impulse, retained fragments, damaged coils, or any pose/velocity injection fail or reduce the score.
candidates.industrial_value: The ODRI shell-preparation procedure explicitly requires these inserts in a robot actuator shell, removal with a tang-break-off tool, and verification that no tang remains inside the part.
candidates.dexterity: The robot must repeatedly align a narrow mandrel with recessed M2.5 inserts, transmit a controlled axial impulse through physical contact, withdraw without snagging the coil, and retrieve millimetre-scale loose fragments. The evidence does not justify requiring two arms.

candidates.asset_plan: Use rigid native PhysX bodies for the shell, installed coils, straight M2.5 mandrel, and free tang fragments. Represent each manufactured notch with a physically loaded breakable constraint; freeze prototype force/impulse/energy thresholds before testing and label them as uncalibrated assumptions. Validate axial fracture, off-axis and insufficient-load controls, excessive-load damage, fragment collision and containment, reset freshness, substep-force measurement, and timestep convergence before YAM integration. The pinned PhysxManager PRE_PHYSICS_STEP and POST_PHYSICS_STEP callbacks are only prospective measurement hooks and require native verification.
candidates.risk: The procedure, insert size, fracture notch, and correct straight-mandrel family are supported. However, the acquired evidence still lacks an independently inspected shell image, shell CAD/STL, or drawing that establishes the four-hole layout, access direction, boss heights, cavity boundaries, and fragment escape paths. The 160 mm module segment length does not establish those local features. Novelty also remains unresolved against the cited punch, hammering, rivet-stem disposal, fracture, snapping, and slide-hammer families.
missing_evidence: Acquired and independently inspected ODRI shell image or pinned CAD/STL establishing insert layout and tool access
Verified local cavity and fragment-escape geometry at faithful scale
Complete current-catalog comparison against pr-1205, pr-142, pr-143, pr-1468, pr-921, pr-1121, pr-1497, and pr-1491
Native component tests establishing plausible fracture scale, physical load coupling, damage behavior, and timestep convergence

candidates.title: Manually tap the M3 encoder and belt-tensioner holes in an ODRI actuator shell
candidates.objective: Hold an M3 tap vertically, start it in each prescribed actuator-shell hole, cut the thread completely through using physical torque and axial control, and withdraw it without cross-threading, stripping, or cracking the printed shell.
candidates.success_conditions: Full success requires all four prescribed M3 holes to accept a representative verification screw through the intended threaded depth, with bounded axis error, no cross-threading, stripped material, cracked shell, stuck tap, or prohibited state writes. Partial credit distinguishes correct starting, partial thread depth, and safe withdrawal.
candidates.industrial_value: The ODRI robot actuator instructions prescribe manual M3 thread cutting for the encoder mount and belt tensioners and warn that printed-part threads can strip.
candidates.dexterity: A robot must establish the thread without cross-threading, maintain tap verticality while producing coupled rotation and feed, periodically regrasp or use a tap holder, sense increasing resistance, and reverse out safely.

candidates.asset_plan: Author a rigid representative tap and shell only after acquiring the referenced hole-location images or CAD. Use a contact-driven helical advancement model whose rotation, axial feed, resistance, and damage arise from physical coupling; validate clean starts, tilted starts, over-torque stripping, jams, reverse extraction, reset behavior, and timestep sensitivity before robot integration.
candidates.risk: The prescribed operation and failure mode are supported, but the acquired text omits the referenced location images and local hole geometry. A credible native thread-cutting interaction may also demand finer contact fidelity than the pinned runtime can stably provide. It is plausibly close to existing fastening, screw-starting, and machining tasks, so novelty is not established.
missing_evidence: Referenced ODRI images or CAD identifying the encoder and tensioner hole locations and access geometry
Shell material and local wall geometry sufficient to bound damage behavior
Native proof that contact-driven tapping can distinguish clean, tilted, stripped, and jammed outcomes without abstract screw-coordinate scoring
Complete novelty comparison with fastening, screw-starting, drilling, and tapping records

candidates.title: Seat five bearings horizontally in an ODRI actuator shell using moderate force
candidates.objective: Place three 8 × 4 × 2 mm transmission bearings and two 32 × 25 × 4 mm output bearings over their correct actuator-shell seats, keep each bearing horizontal, and press each fully into its light press-fit without cocking or damaging the shell.
candidates.success_conditions: Full success requires every bearing in its correct seat, fully seated and within a frozen angular tolerance for two seconds, with no cocked bearing, wrong-seat placement, excessive press force, cracked seat, deformed bearing, dropped component, or direct state write. Safe alignment and partial seating receive partial credit.
candidates.industrial_value: The ODRI actuator-shell preparation procedure specifies the bearing dimensions, describes a light press-fit, requires horizontal installation, and identifies the prepared shell as part of robot actuator assembly.
candidates.dexterity: The robot must handle two substantially different bearing sizes, align thin rings to close-fitting seats, regulate insertion force, detect cocking, and recover safely before damage.

candidates.asset_plan: Use rigid bearing rings and a representative printed shell with physically modeled seat interference. Freeze uncited clearance, friction, angular tolerance, and damage thresholds as prototype assumptions. Before YAM integration, test free alignment, correct seating, cocking, wrong-size placement, excessive-force damage, removal force, reset freshness, and timestep convergence.
candidates.risk: Bearing sizes and handling requirements are well supported, but the acquired record contains only text placeholders for the bearing-location images. Seat diameters, depths, access, and interference are not established. Without that geometry this could collapse into a generic peg/ring insertion task, and current-catalog novelty has not been demonstrated.
missing_evidence: Acquired bearing-location images or shell CAD/STL with seat diameters, depths, spacing, and approach access
A defensible representative interference/contact model and native press-fit validation
Complete novelty comparison against bearing insertion, press-fit, ring placement, and generic insertion tasks
Evidence that the resulting objective differs in ability and outcome rather than only part geometry

selection_reason: No candidate is ready. The strongest candidate is ODRI M2.5 HELICOIL tang removal, but the prior failure remains unresolved: acquired evidence still does not establish the actual shell’s local insert-access and fragment-escape geometry, and no native fracture/contact validation exists. Selecting it as ready would contradict the requirement that a ready candidate have no critical missing evidence. The tapping and bearing alternatives are industrially grounded but have still larger geometry, physics, and novelty gaps.
